title: How to Remember 15 Synonyms for HAPPY With One Story (Easy Memory Challenge)
description:
Ten words for HAPPY in a plain list, then one silly story. How many can you remember each time?

1. Watch the list and pause: write down every word you remember (score 1).
2. Watch the story and pause again: write down every word you recall, in order (score 2).
3. Comment your two scores: list vs story.

On the way you climb a ladder from a little bit happy to extremely happy: content, glad, pleased, chuffed, cheerful, upbeat, joyful, delighted, thrilled, over the moon, overjoyed, on cloud nine, elated, jubilant, ecstatic, with what each word means and when to use it (formal, informal, British).

More ways to say "happy": https://anotherwordfor.net/another-word-for-happy/

#synonyms #englishvocabulary #memorychallenge

language_approval.notes: Full pre-generation gate of script.md, focus.txt, meta.json (S1 HAPPY). CTA fixed: anotherwordfor.net/another-word-for-happy/ is HTTP 200 but has NO example sentences, no search box and does not list chuffed/over the moon -> voice says 'look up "another word for happy" on anotherwordfor.net', description links that page. on cloud nine: removed invented 'for a long time / long afterwards' sense (Cambridge: extremely happy and excited). jubilant: 'triumphant joy' (noun phrase, B2+) -> 'very happy and celebrating (a win)', register 'mostly written' not 'formal' (no formal label in learner dictionaries). joyful: 'sounds a little written' (unidiomatic) -> 'more common in writing'; elated recap likewise. upbeat line 'lunch will be even better' -> 'Never mind, I'll get an even better one!'. over the moon: 'some news' -> 'good news'. thrilled recap 'very happy and excited'. Hook: dropped 'exactly' (ladder is approximate). content: pronunciation cue con-TENT added (spoken + focus). No memory statistics, no 'most people'. 973 spoken words (~7 min incl. pauses). Not checked: generated video/transcript; title keeps '15' as specified in the runbook although the hook says 'ten' (spoils the reveal slightly, not a language error).
